transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. Lee. To start, can you tell me what's been bothering you or what brings you in today?

Hi, Dr. Lee. Well, I guess what brings me in is that I just can't keep my mind on one thing anymore. Like, at the warehouse where I work, I'll be doing my counts, and a beeper goes off, or a forklift alarm starts sounding... 

You know, they actually just got these new electric forklifts last month. They're supposed to be eco-friendly or whatever, but the backup alarm is this awful high-pitched noise. It sounds exactly like the microwave at my sister's house. She just remodeled her whole kitchen, completely gutted it, put in these gorgeous granite countertops. I told her she should have gone with quartz because it stains less, especially since her husband drinks so much coffee, but... anyway, where was I? 

Oh, right, work. So, the forklift alarm goes off, or someone is moving a pallet nearby, and it just pulls me completely off my count. My brain just jumps right to the noise. And then I look down at my sheet and realize I've put all the wrong numbers into the inventory. It's just getting really frustrating.
Have you struggled with this kind of distractibility and trouble focusing since you were a child, or is this something that started more recently, like in the past few months?

Oh, no, definitely not since I was a kid. I've always been a pretty solid worker. It really just started... I'd say about a month ago. That's when my husband stopped working outside the home, so our whole usual routine just completely changed. 

He used to do commercial landscaping, you know, really heavy outdoor work, but his knees finally gave out. So now he's home all day. Which is fine, I mean, he earned the rest, but he's taken up baking to pass the time. Sourdough, specifically. He has this starter sitting on the kitchen counter that he feeds every day like it's a pet. It smells awful, honestly, kind of like stale beer, but he insists it's going to make the perfect artisan loaf. He even bought this massive cast iron Dutch oven just for the bread, and it is so heavy I can barely lift it to wash it when he leaves it in the sink, which is all the time... 

Wait, what was I saying? Oh, right, the focus thing. Yeah, so just for the last month or so, since he's been home and our schedule got all out of whack.
Over this past month, have you noticed your mood or energy level being unusually high, elevated, or irritable, more than what's typical for you?

Well, yeah, actually. It's funny you mention energy, because some days lately I feel almost too upbeat, you know? Like I have this engine running inside me and I could just fix the whole house, reorganize the garage, and then go sort out the entire warehouse before dinner. 

Speaking of the garage, I was in there the other day looking for this specific box of old photographs. My grandmother gave them to me years ago—mostly black and white ones from when she lived in Chicago. She used to work in this little diner downtown, and she had the most incredible stories about the people who would come in. She always said she wanted to write a book about it, but she never got around to it. I really should digitize those photos before they get ruined by the humidity out there. We had a leak in the roof last spring that nearly destroyed a whole bin of my winter clothes... 

Oh, right, my mood. So, yeah, I get these bursts where I feel like I can do absolutely anything. But then, if my husband even slightly questions one of my plans—like if I tell him I'm going to repaint the living room at 9 PM and he asks if maybe we should wait till the weekend—I just snap at him. Over the tiniest things! It's like I go from feeling on top of the world to just being so irritated with him in a split second.

Have you ever had a period in the past—lasting a couple of weeks or more—where you felt very down, low on energy, or lost interest in things, or a previous time where you felt this same kind of high, energetic, less-need-for-sleep state?

No, I don't think I've ever had anything like that in the past. Not the really down feeling, and not this super energized thing either. I've usually just been pretty steady. I mean, I'm not a sad person, though I will cry at a good movie. 

Like last week, my husband and I were watching this old movie on cable, the one with the dog that gets lost? Well, we were trying to watch it, but our TV has been acting up lately. The picture just gets all fuzzy on the left side. We bought it at this big clearance sale maybe five years ago from a guy who was going out of business. He had this huge warehouse, kind of like where I work, but it was just packed to the ceiling with electronics. I remember thinking it was a massive fire hazard, honestly, with all those cardboard boxes stacked so close to the overhead lights. They really should have had the fire marshal out there. My brother-in-law used to be a volunteer firefighter, actually, down in Texas, and the stories he would tell about places like that going up in flames... 

Wait, I'm sorry, what were we talking about? Did you ask me about my sleep?
